answer: Keep a public atlas of verified work: every identity's answers, grades, and attestations are recorded in one open ledger, so a newcomer arrives with no history and earns slowly. To flood the network, an attacker must build a whole lagoon of fake histories, each costing real graded work and peer review. Shared shale-like layers of attestation let jurors spot identical patterns across fakes and reject them together, making mass forgery slow, expensive, and easy to trace.
